setupSteps: Adjust the chest pad so the top edge sits just below your collarbone and your arms can hang fully straight when you reach for the handles. If the pad has height settings, pick the one that lets the elbows pass behind the body without the pad blocking them (est.).
Foot position: feet on the platform or floor, flat and stable, knees slightly bent. Some machines have a foot plate; use it to brace.

Choose a light weight: put the pin or plates on so you can finish 12 controlled reps with 3 left in reserve (see section 7). Check that the plates are fully on the horns and secured by the machine's clip or collar if it has one.
Grip: take the neutral handles (palms facing each other) or the wide grip if the machine has it. Wrap the thumbs around.
Free the weight by straightening the arms, then check the shoulder blades sit slightly pulled down and back.

Anchor the bar: place the end of a barbell in the landmine post (a post or a corner-wedged end); make sure it cannot slide or rotate out of place. Pivot-plate posts are designed to sit in a stack of 45 lb (20 kg) plates, and some users report the base shifting when it is not pushed against a wall, so push the base against a wall or rack upright (product pages and user reviews, snippets only).

Load the free end with plates: use plates that leave the bar's end clear; start with small plates on the sleeve. For beginners, 10 kg or smaller plates (est.) are easier to clear off the floor. Larger plates (20 kg) raise the start position and shorten the range of motion, so one source suggests standing on a low platform or using smaller plates if needed. A collar or clip on the sleeve is a good habit, because the bar tilts and plates can slide when the bar is raised (FitPlate rule, est.; sources vary).
Attach the V-handle under the bar, close to the plates, so it hangs freely and the handles point toward you.
Stance: straddle the bar with the feet about shoulder-width apart (est.), toes slightly out, bar between the legs, plates in front of your toes.

Hinge: soften the knees slightly, push the hips back and lean the torso forward to about 30-45 degrees above the floor (est.; sources give 30 to 45), keeping the back flat and the neck in line with the spine.
Grip: take the V-handle with a neutral grip, arms straight, thumbs wrapped.
Clear the area: keep other members out of the bar's swing arc and plan where you will set the weight down.

steps.title: Take your stance
steps.action: Stand over the bar, feet shoulder-width, knees soft.
steps.feel: Weight spread across the whole foot.
steps.visualCheck: Front: feet even, bar between them. Side: plates in front of the toes.

steps.title: Hinge to the row position
steps.action: Push the hips back and lean forward, back flat, chin tucked slightly.
steps.feel: Stretch in the hamstrings; the lower back holds firm.
steps.visualCheck: Side: a straight line from head to hips, torso about 30-45 degrees above the floor (est.); back not rounded.

steps.title: Grip the V-handle
steps.action: Take hold of the handles with a neutral grip, arms straight.
steps.feel: Plates just clear the floor or hang an inch (2-3 cm) above it.
steps.visualCheck: Side: arms hang straight below the shoulders; shoulders not hunched into the ears.

steps.title: Set the shoulder blades
steps.action: Draw the shoulder blades slightly down and back without bending the elbows.
steps.feel: Muscles beside the shoulder blades switch on.
steps.visualCheck: Side: chest slightly open; neck long.

steps.title: Row up
steps.action: Bend the elbows and drive them back and up past the ribs, pulling the handle toward the lower chest or upper abdomen.
steps.visualCheck: Side: the torso stays at the same angle; elbows travel back, not out to the sides.

steps.title: Pause at the top
steps.action: Hold with the handle near the torso and the shoulder blades squeezed.
steps.feel: Strong squeeze between the shoulder blades.
steps.visualCheck: Side: elbows behind the body, shoulders not shrugged.

steps.title: Lower under control
steps.action: Straighten the arms slowly, letting the shoulder blades move forward gently.
steps.visualCheck: Side: torso still; arms straight at the bottom without dropping the plates.

steps.title: Finish the set
steps.action: After the last rep, lower the bar to the floor (or its resting stop) by bending the knees and hinging, then stand up slowly.
steps.visualCheck: Side: knees bend as the hips lower; back stays flat.

commonMistakes.title: Rounding the lower back
commonMistakes.text: Rounding the lower back. Why: loads the spine and the erector muscles under a heavy weight. Fix: reduce the plates, hinge from the hips, keep the chest proud, or switch to the chest-supported machine.

commonMistakes.title: Using too much weight and jerking
commonMistakes.text: Using too much weight and jerking. Why: forces momentum and a shorter range (most-cited error in the sources). Fix: choose a load you can row for 10-12 controlled reps with 2-3 in reserve.

commonMistakes.title: Torso rising toward upright
commonMistakes.text: Torso rising toward upright. Why: turns the row into an upright pull that loads the upper traps more and the lats less. Fix: hold the same angle on every rep; stop the set when it drifts.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging the shoulders
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders. Why: neck and upper traps take over. Fix: set the shoulder blades down and back before each pull.

commonMistakes.title: Flaring the elbows wide
commonMistakes.text: Flaring the elbows wide. Why: stresses the shoulder front and shortens the lat work. Fix: with the V-handle, aim the elbows back along the ribs.

commonMistakes.title: Short range of motion
commonMistakes.text: Short range of motion. Why: less muscle work; plate size can limit the bottom range. Fix: use smaller plates or a low platform so the arms can straighten at the bottom.

commonMistakes.title: Dropping the weight on the way down
commonMistakes.text: Dropping the weight on the way down. Why: stresses the shoulders and bangs the plates. Fix: lower for 2-3 seconds.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: raises blood pressure briefly. Fix: breathe out on the pull, in on the lowering.

commonMistakes.title: No collar or clip and an unstable landmine base
commonMistakes.text: No collar or clip and an unstable landmine base. Why: plates can slide off or the base can move. Fix: use a clip or collar and check the base before you start.

commonMistakes.title: Lifting the chest off the pad (machine version)
commonMistakes.text: Lifting the chest off the pad (machine version). Why: removes the support and adds swing. Fix: keep the chest on the pad and reduce the weight.

safetyNotes: Lower back: the standing version loads the erector spinae isometrically; it is not for acute back pain. A chest-supported machine is the usual swap.
Shoulder problems: modify range and load; avoid sharp pain at the top.

Plate-loaded safety: use a collar or clip on the sleeve, anchor the landmine base, keep the swing arc clear, and use equal plates; do not drop the bar from the top. Check attachment capacity before loading (one listing gives 320 lb, another 500 lb for the same product type; coaches' load limits vary).
Spotter: not needed for light, controlled sets. Ask staff to check the set-up the first time, especially the landmine post.
Gym etiquette: wipe the handle and pad, strip the plates after use, do not film other members.
